headline: Litigation charges, weak chicken prices crush earnings
summary_short: Pilgrim's Pride's Q2 FY2026 (three months ended June 28, 2026) net sales were roughly flat at $4,626.2 million (-2.8% y/y), but net income collapsed 96.2% y/y to $13.4 million ($0.06 diluted EPS) as weak US commodity chicken pricing and Broiler Antitrust Litigation settlement costs crushed margins.
summary_long: Gross profit fell 52.5% y/y to $339.8 million as US commodity chicken prices stayed below historical averages amid industry oversupply (USDA estimated Q2 ready-to-cook production +4.5% y/y), while costs per pound rose on higher live-operations, grain, and utility costs. SG&A jumped 32.9% y/y on legal settlement and defense costs; the filing discloses $155.4 million of H1 2026 Broiler Antitrust Litigation settlements with Broiler Opt Outs (cumulative $838.5 million to date). Operating income fell 87.1% y/y to $66.0 million; net interest expense rose 46.6% on a $17.5 million loss from tendering 2033 Senior Notes. Cash fell to $388.8 million from $849.0 million a year ago as capex nearly doubled to $254.2 million. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Company-disclosed: US net sales fell 6.1% on a 6.6% drop in sales price per pound from unfavorable market pricing versus historical averages, partly offset by 0.5% higher volume; Europe and Mexico grew on FX and volume.

Company-disclosed: US cost per pound rose on higher live-operations, grain, grower pay, depreciation and utilities costs, compounding the lower US sales price per pound from weak commodity chicken pricing.

Company-disclosed: US SG&A rose on higher legal settlement expense and legal defense costs; the filing separately discloses $155.4M of H1 2026 Broiler Antitrust Litigation settlement expense (Note 17), on top of the gross-profit decline.
Derived-arithmetic: EBITDA fell less steeply than operating income (-69.1% vs -87.1% y/y) because the D&A add-back is unaffected by the litigation and pricing pressure hitting operating income.

Derived-arithmetic: net income fell in step with the operating income collapse, compounded by a 46.6% rise in net interest expense; income tax expense fell proportionally less, keeping the effective rate near prior levels.
Derived-arithmetic: diluted EPS fell 96.0% y/y, tracking the 96.2% net income decline; weighted diluted shares were essentially unchanged y/y.

Company-disclosed: interest expense increased primarily due to a $17.5 million loss on early extinguishment of debt from the tender offer on the Senior Notes due 2033, adding to the operating income decline.
